# Vendored crates

**gpui-pre-windows** is GPUI's Windows platform at 0.3.12, from crates.io, under its Apache-2.0 licence. Four changes are made, marked `loom:`. The third, in `src/shaders.hlsl`, draws a rotated image, and the fourth, `load_pan_cursor` in `src/util.rs`, shows the system's pan cursors; both are described with **gpui-pre** below.

In `src/platform.rs`, the vsync thread only tells windows that are on screen to paint. Before the change it told every window to paint at every vblank, so the app's main thread woke 240 times a second while minimised, which cost 68–90 ms of CPU a second. Once every window has been off screen for a second, as when loom is in the tray, the thread looks five times a second rather than at every vblank. It waits that second because a window that's opening isn't on screen until its first frame, and the frames after that wait on this thread: without the wait, the chat showed up to 200 ms later at start.

A window on screen is told to paint only when it has something new to draw (`FrameDemand` in `src/window.rs`): GPUI says so through the window's `frame_waker` and `schedule_frame`, as it does for macOS's display link. A window shown and idle used to be woken at every vblank to find it had nothing to draw, 28–42 ms of CPU a second. While a touchpad gesture runs it's still told at every vblank, since Direct Manipulation is pumped from each paint (`src/direct_manipulation.rs`), and every window is told four times a second regardless, in case a frame GPUI put off isn't asked for again.

To move to a newer GPUI, copy that version's crate here and make the same changes again. If upstream has made them already, drop the patch from `../Cargo.toml` instead.

**gpui-base** is GPUI Base at 0.10.0, from crates.io, under its Apache-2.0 licence. Six changes are made, marked `loom:`. An inline `<span style="color: #rrggbb; font-weight: 500">` in Markdown gives its text that color and weight (`TextMark`'s `color` and `weight` in `src/text/node.rs`, read in `src/text/format/markdown.rs`). The chat draws an agent's name that way where a message mentions it, in the agent's colour. And a link whose text has its own colour keeps it, with no underline (`decorate_link` in `src/text/node.rs`), and under the pointer has a light background of that colour (`Inline::paint_link_hover` in `src/text/inline.rs`), so an agent's name is a link to its chat that still reads as the agent. The third: an emoji the chat draws as a picture, an image whose source starts with `loom-emoji` (PLAN.md, "Emoji"), is one character to the selection, as an inline object is, and copies as its alt text, the emoji itself or `:name:`, where any other picture copies as nothing. It has the selection's colour across its line's height once a drag passes its middle, a double click on it selects it alone and a triple click its line (`EmojiPicture` in `src/text/inline_object.rs`, which `src/text/inline_flow.rs` puts around it), and copying takes it whole (`loom_emoji_alt`, read by `Paragraph::selected_text`, `selected_source_range`, `selected_markdown` and `text` in `src/text/node.rs`). A paragraph that has one is laid out as a line, a paragraph of emoji alone too, so its pictures take part in the selection. The fourth: a picture inside a line of text shows the link tooltip of the link it sits in, as a word of a link does (`image_element` in `src/text/inline_flow.rs`), so the chat can show an emoji's card under the pointer. The fifth: an input tells a token's renderer the colour it paints its selection with while that selection shows over the token, its window active and it or its selection popup focused (`InlineTokenContext::selection` in `src/input/base/token_presentation.rs`), since the input leaves a token's background to the renderer: loom's composer paints its pieces with it, as the words beside them. The sixth: an inline element can let its line cut it (`InlineElement::cut_to_fit` in `src/text/inline_element.rs`): one wider than a whole line is given the width its fit says for the room left where it starts, or starts the next line, and is built again at that width (`cut_wide_objects` in `src/text/inline_flow.rs`, `MeasuredInlineObject::element` in `src/text/inline_object.rs`), where before it ran past the line's end; a card's pill cuts its title so. To move to a newer GPUI Base, copy that version's crate here and make the same changes again, or drop the patch if upstream has a way to colour a span and a link, select an inline picture, colour a selected token and cut an inline element to its line.

**gpui-pre** is GPUI at 0.3.12, with its renderers **gpui-pre-apple** (Metal) and **gpui-pre-wgpu** (Linux), from crates.io, under their Apache-2.0 licence. Four changes are made, marked `loom:`. The first, across them and the Windows renderer above: an image can be drawn moved by a `TransformationMatrix`, as an SVG icon already could, so the chat can tilt a message's pictures. `PolychromeSprite` gains a `transformation` as its last field (`src/scene.rs`), which `Window::paint_image_transformed` sets (`src/window.rs`); `paint_image` and emoji pass the unit matrix. `TransformationMatrix::rotation_about` builds a rotation about a point, and `Transformation::into_matrix` (`src/elements/svg.rs`) is public. A moved image is culled and ordered against other primitives by the box around its moved corners. Each renderer's polychrome sprite shader (`shaders.hlsl`, `shaders.metal`, `shaders.wgsl` with its WebGL loader in `shaders_webgl.wgsl`) places the corners with the matrix, as the monochrome one does, and rounds the corners in the image's own space rather than on screen. A moved image's quad is a pixel larger each way, sampling the tile's edge there, so its edges are smoothed on both sides. An image that isn't moved takes the same path as before and is drawn to the bit as it was. gpui-pre-apple builds its shader structs from its own copy of GPUI's sources in `vendor/gpui`, so `scene.rs`, `window.rs` and `platform.rs` there are kept the same as gpui-pre's. To move to a newer GPUI, copy that version's crates here and make the same changes again, or drop the patches if upstream can draw a transformed image, show pan cursors, measure wrapped text and cancel a tooltip on a press as below.

The second change, also marked `loom:`, shows the cursors of a browser's middle-button scrolling. `PanCursor` (`src/platform.rs`) is up and down at rest, up, or down. `Window::set_pan_cursor` shows one over the whole window, ahead of every `CursorStyle`, until it's set to `None`, and isn't part of a frame, so it shows at once. `Window::hovered_cursor_style` gives the cursor style under the pointer, which loom reads so the middle button leaves links and buttons alone. They aren't `CursorStyle` variants because every platform matches `CursorStyle` whole, so gpui-pre-linux and gpui-pre-web would have to be vendored too. Instead, `Platform::set_pan_cursor` defaults to the nearest resize cursor, and Windows and the Mac draw their own. Windows (above) loads user32's pan cursors, resources without names: 32652 at rest, 32655 up, 32656 down. The Mac has none, so **gpui-pre-macos** draws them.

The third change, also marked `loom:`, is in how text is measured (`TextLayout::layout` in `src/elements/text.rs`). Asked for its size with no width to wrap at, as a flex item's own width is found, text answered with its last layout whatever width that was wrapped at, so a reply's bubble, sized by its words, took the narrow width of an earlier pass as its own; with gpui-base keeping a text's layout from frame to frame, a reply stayed wrapped a few words wide in a chat at its narrowest. Now a layout wrapped at a width answers such a question only when nothing in it wrapped, and otherwise the text is measured again without wrapping, as upstream already does for truncated text. `wrap_tests` in `src/app.rs` checks it.

The fourth change, also marked `loom:`, is in when a tooltip shows (`clear_active_tooltip_if_not_hoverable` in `src/elements/div.rs`). A press or a scroll took away a tooltip that showed, but not one still waiting out its delay, which came up once the delay ended: right-clicking an emoji in the chat before its name card showed put the card over the menu the right-click opened. Now a press or a scroll cancels a tooltip waiting to show too.

**gpui-pre-macos** is GPUI's macOS platform at 0.3.12, from crates.io, under its Apache-2.0 licence. One change is made, marked `loom:`: `set_pan_cursor` shows a pan cursor through the window's cursor rects, as `set_cursor_style` shows a style. `src/pan_cursor.rs` draws each the way Windows draws its own, black triangles and a dot with a 1-point white edge on a 32-point square, into an image with a 1× and a 2× bitmap, and makes the `NSCursor` once. Its tests don't build, as upstream's didn't, without GPUI's test support. To move to a newer GPUI, copy that version's crate here and make the same change again.
